target.title: fix(agents): strip MiniMax stream-boundary marker from transport payload text
target.body:
## Summary

Closes #104403 — a MiniMax-portal stream-boundary marker (`ESC[e~[` / `[e~[`) leaked into `assistantTexts[0]`, the trajectory JSONL, and the next-turn `finalPromptText`, so every assistant reply ended with a stray token.

## Root cause

`sanitizeTransportPayloadText` only stripped malformed surrogate pairs. The MiniMax portal injects a terminal/escape stream-boundary marker into assistant text on the anthropic-messages transport; nothing removed it, so it propagated to every downstream consumer.

## Fix

- `src/agents/transport-stream-shared.ts`: `sanitizeTransportPayloadText` now also strips ANSI/terminal escape sequences (reusing `stripAnsiSequences`) and the MiniMax boundary marker. Both the anthropic-messages and openai-responses transports call this helper, so the noise is removed at the transport layer where it actually enters `assistantTexts`.
- This complements the channel-layer stripping in #105243 rather than duplicating it.

## Verification

- `vitest run --pool forks src/agents/transport-stream-shared.test.ts` — 22 passed (incl. new regression test for the ESC-prefixed marker, the bare `[e~[` form, repeated markers, and ordinary ANSI color codes).
- `oxlint` clean (0/0), `oxfmt --check` clean on the changed file.

## Note

The reporter also referenced an attached report with a suggested code diff; the core defect (marker not stripped at the transport layer) is addressed here. If maintainers want the marker handled exclusively at the channel layer instead, this transport-layer strip is harmless and defensively correct.
